about: Accepted faults and author decisions collected while finishing V15 chapters 1 to 8 (2026-10-01). Art faults here used their correction attempts or sit in approved art; each needs an author decision (accept, or regenerate later).

items.fault: Accepted fault for the author list: Ibrahim still shows a faint diagonal scar mark on his RIGHT cheek (the image-left side of his face, in front of his visible ear). The v03 edit made it lighter than in v02, but it was not removed, and the LEFT-side scar is not shown.

Accepted faults for the author's list (v03, the latest edit, is v02 with these marks only slightly softened): (1) Ibrahim's forehead ash still reads as three soft horizontal white stripes just below the turban, not one thumb smear. (2) The seated official on the far platform still has a small dark-red dot at the centre of his forehead; the script says no forehead marks. (3) Minor: Ibrahim's scar is a thin pale line on his visible LEFT cheek that runs from below the ear toward the corner of the moustache rather than down to the jaw. It is on the correct side.

Accepted faults for the author list. (1) Ibrahim still has two short pale-white dashes on his RIGHT cheek (screen-left, just below the eye). The v03 edit did not remove them. (2) His forehead ash is a small pale rectangular patch with faint horizontal striping, just below the turban, not one soft thumb smear. This is better than v02's two distinct white stripes but still not a smear.

v03 is acceptable and matches the evening lamplit hall. The setting is right: a dark carved back wall, open brass oil lamps on chains and a standing brass lamp, an unlettered silver-conch-on-red standard, bare-headed Nair guards with topknots and crossed belts, and topknotted seated men. The official is seen from behind with a topknot and white shoulder cloth. Nagoji is correct: clean chin, thick curled moustache, hair tied back, cream tunic-shirt, bandaged wrists, barefoot, eyes on the official. Ibrahim wears no coat, only the cream vest over a white shirt and white mundu, with his turban and grey-flecked beard. The plain ochre wall band across the top is clear for the three balloons. For the author list: (1) Ibrahim's forehead ash is still two pale horizontal stripes, not one faint smear. v03 is acceptable and is now evening. The brass oil lamps light the room, the walls are warm ochre, and the far-left window shows a dusk sky with palm silhouettes, so it matches 8.1 and the earlier hall panels. The official is at the right on his raised seat, at a readable size, with a slight smile, a topknot, a clean chin, a bare torso and the stylus over the leaf. Nagoji makes a measured standing bow in the left foreground: clean chin, curled moustache, gold ear ornament, hair tied at the nape, bandaged wrists. Ibrahim stands a step behind him with no coat. The large plain wall beside and above the official is free for both official balloons. The captions can sit on the wall between Nagoji's lowered head and the pillar, or on the floor below. items.fault: A background prisoner has Nagoji's markers (curly hair, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud); minor (r13 review).
Keshavrao's arms are flung wide with no chain between his wrist manacles; the chapter's irons call for a forearm-long chain (r9 review).
The broadside wave beat reads weakly: a level, untilted hold rather than men thrown sideways (r9 review).

Panels 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 3.5 are narrowed to about 78 percent of the column and centred while 3.4 runs full width; choose tighter crops to fill the width, or one shared width for every panel on a page (r9 review).

The caption 'The dungeon had scraped that away.' sits across the Chaul memory inset (young Keshavrao on the bay horse). Page 5 cannot fit its five panels' lettering: the script makes 5.4 full width and 5.5 the full-width, tallest panel, which leaves 5.2 about 66 pt tall. Options: accept the overlap, let 5.5 be shorter than its full-width height, or shorten or move one 5.2 caption.
'Horses would hate this.' now reads last at the bottom left of 3.3, in script order, but no longer sits on the feet inset it jokes about.

Keshavrao faces the camera and turns fully to stare at Nagoji; the script wants him seen from behind, head turned only a few degrees, eyes forward ('a friend who will not look back'), right hand curled at the hip round an absent hilt. Needs a regeneration if the author wants the beat.
Page 1's tiers have three different widths and none fills the column (same question as chapter 3 page 3): tighter crops to fill the width, or one shared width per page.
A tiny background musketeer in a blue coat and gold-edged tricorne reads as a Dutch blue-coat, against the rule for Portuguese guards; recolour or paint out on a later pass.

The brand is drawn differently in each panel (angry puckered patch in 3.2, lacy blotch in 5.4, four pale curved lines like whip marks in 6.5). A later pass could redraw 6.5 (and 5.4) as a paler version of the 3.2 patch.
A small white lace-like pattern on the outer side of Nagoji's left forearm reads as a scuff or salt crust at print size; clean it back to plain skin on a retouch pass.
The background wreck shows bare ribs close inshore, like an old rotted hulk rather than the fresh wreck of 2.4.

items.fault: After two correction attempts: the hand at the belt is drawn as a right hand (thumb on the inner side, next to the buckle) on the LEFT arm, and the nails do not clearly show ridges. Logged for the author (v02 has the brand near the elbow on the outer forearm instead).

Script 12.4 now starts 'Full width.' (accepted revision, backup scripts/CHAPTER-07-SCRIPT.md.backup-pre-124-fullwidth): at half width beside 12.3 there was no room in the dusk sky for Ibrahim's long line without covering Nagoji. Revert if you prefer the pairing; the line would then need shortening.
The child beside the whispering girl still wears an olive short-sleeved stitched top (the girl's own blouse was fixed); an edit could drape her in cream cloth too.

The top tier of page 5 is ragged: 5.2 is fitted to its art's aspect and centred, so it is shorter than 5.1 beside it, with cream bands above and below. Same question as chapter 2 page 1 and chapter 3 page 3.

decided: 2026-10-02: Nagoji's ear ornament is the small flush gold stud (bible). From chapter 9 the prompts and selection enforce it; panels already picked in chapters 1 to 8 that show a small hanging drop are a known deviation, listed here for a later pass if wanted.
